tagline: Around the Kilkenny woods through the old paper towns.
intro: The loop starts in Lancaster near the Connecticut River and runs up US 3 to Groveton, where NH 110 turns east to Stark, on the Upper Ammonoosuc. It comes over to the Androscoggin at Milan and follows that river down to Berlin and Gorham, then heads west on US 2 through Randolph and Jefferson, with the Presidential Range in view, all the way around the Kilkenny District of the White Mountain National Forest.
This was paper country. Berlin's mills drew workers from Norway, Russia, Finland, Quebec and farther, and even the German prisoners held at Camp Stark from 1944 cut wood for them.

moments.title: Stark Covered Bridge
moments.text: The much-photographed white bridge over the Upper Ammonoosuc was once washed away along with its granite pier, survived, and was set back on its abutments.

moments.title: Nansen Ski Jump
moments.text: Built in 1936 just north of Berlin, the Big Nansen was the largest ski jump in the eastern United States for almost fifty years and held the first Olympic trials in 1938.

moments.title: Randolph
moments.text: Around Randolph the road looks up into King Ravine, a glacial cirque on Mount Adams.
